ai.definition: On-device AI refers to the deployment of machine learning models directly on the user's device, such as smartphones or IoT devices, rather than relying on a centralized cloud infrastructure.
ai.howItWorks: These models are trained offline and then deployed onto the end-user device. They can process data locally without sending it to the cloud for analysis, which significantly reduces latency and enhances privacy by keeping sensitive information within the user's control.
ai.problemSolved: On-device AI addresses the challenges of high latency in cloud-based systems and the potential risks associated with transmitting personal data over networks, including security breaches and privacy concerns.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and deploying trained machine learning models onto various types of devices. This requires optimizing models for resource-constrained environments to ensure efficient use of memory, processing power, and battery life.
ai.buildProcess: Building on-device AI solutions starts with training the model offline using large datasets. The next step is to optimize the model for deployment by reducing its size and computational requirements while maintaining acceptable performance levels. Finally, the optimized model is integrated into the device's software stack.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the development of efficient algorithms, optimization techniques, and hardware adaptations for resource-constrained environments. Additionally, ensuring strong privacy and security measures adds to the overall cost.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to grow as more devices are equipped with sufficient computational resources, and user privacy concerns continue to rise.
ai.regulation: Regulations around data privacy and security will play a significant role in the adoption of on-device AI. Compliance with standards like GDPR or CCPA may be required depending on the region and industry.
ai.risks: Risks include potential vulnerabilities in locally deployed models, limited model accuracy due to resource constraints, and challenges in maintaining consistent performance across different device types.
ai.profitability: Profitability is dependent on the specific use case and market. While it can reduce cloud costs for certain applications, it may also require higher initial investment in development and optimization.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments could focus on improving model efficiency, enhancing privacy features, and expanding support for more complex machine learning tasks directly on devices.

subsystems.name: Model
subsystems.role: the compressed neural network that performs the actual task.

subsystems.name: Inference runtime
subsystems.role: executes the model on the device and routes work to the best processor.

subsystems.name: Hardware accelerator
subsystems.role: runs the heavy matrix maths efficiently within a phone's power budget.

subsystems.name: Memory and storage manager
subsystems.role: fits model weights and intermediate data into limited RAM.

subsystems.name: OS integration and APIs
subsystems.role: standard interface for apps to request inference and manage power.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline
subsystems.role: captures and preprocesses sensor input before inference.

buildSteps.title: Train a large model
buildSteps.detail: Cloud GPUs train a neural network on massive datasets to reach high accuracy, without yet worrying about size.

buildSteps.title: Compress the model
buildSteps.detail: Pruning removes weak connections, quantization reduces weight precision (for example from 32-bit to 8-bit), and knowledge distillation trains a smaller model to mimic the large one.

buildSteps.title: Convert to a device format
buildSteps.detail: Tools such as TensorFlow Lite, Core ML or ONNX convert the trained graph into a compact file the phone can load.

buildSteps.title: Optimize for hardware
buildSteps.detail: Operations are mapped to NPU, GPU or DSP kernels, memory layout is tuned, and the runtime chooses which delegate runs each part.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into the app
buildSteps.detail: The app calls the runtime API, feeds in camera or microphone data, and receives the model's output.

buildSteps.title: Test on real devices
buildSteps.detail: Engineers measure latency, power draw, thermal throttling and accuracy across many phone models.

buildSteps.title: Ship and update
buildSteps.detail: The model is bundled with the app or downloaded over the air; some apps also fine-tune locally using federated learning so raw data never leaves the device.

prerequisites.why: dedicated neural accelerators run inference fast enough for real time without draining the battery.
quantization, pruning and distillation shrink models so they fit in phone memory and run within power limits.
they provide the software layer that translates a model into operations the phone's hardware can execute.
keeping data local protects users, but model theft and adversarial inputs remain active concerns.
sustained AI workloads can overheat a phone and cut battery life, so scheduling and throttling are essential.

pathway.milestone: specialized on-device models for vision, speech and translation, such as face unlock and offline captions
pathway.unlocks: fast, private features that work without a network connection.

pathway.milestone: small language models of a few billion parameters running locally for summarization and assistants
pathway.unlocks: conversational AI that is always available and keeps text on the device.

pathway.milestone: personalization through federated learning and on-device fine-tuning
pathway.unlocks: models that adapt to each user without sending raw data to the cloud.

pathway.milestone: continuous, multimodal on-device agents that see, hear and reason locally
pathway.unlocks: rich ambient computing with low latency and strong privacy.
